messages:
Incident Bot: Pager P-4592 triggered - PROD: elevated API error rate detected (>5%). Auto-opened incident channel.

Emma (oncall): I'm taking initial triage. Paging @Raj and @Lisa, will gather early impact.

Raj (eng-sre): Looking at traces now. Cluster seems healthy. Error patterns point to CI/CD failures: multiple GH Actions runner errors and package fetch failures from npm.pkg.github.com.

Lisa (platform): CI alert: runners can't fetch actions or packages. GitHub status shows 'Partial Outage' for Actions & Packages - https://www.githubstatus.com/ (link).

Chris (deploy): Hotfix pipeline aborted: actions/checkout failing. Logs show DNS and 502/504 to npm.pkg.github.com. Example: ```Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND npm.pkg.github.com``` Retrying the job doesn't help.

Emma (oncall): Impact assessment: serving currently stable, but hotfix deployment is blocked — Dedicated customers expecting patches could be affected. Maria, advise on status messaging for customers.

Maria (product): Draft status: "Deployment pipelines are impaired due to a third-party outage (GitHub Actions / Packages). Serving is unaffected. We're executing a workaround to allow hotfix releases." Notify enterprise customers on the watchlist.

DevOps: Can we pivot to self-hosted runners and a different registry? We have a few self-hosted runners but package registry calls still point at GitHub Packages.

Raj (eng-sre): Two-pronged mitigation: 1) register more self-hosted runners and 2) serve private packages from an internal mirror (Artifactory/verdaccio) or cached artifacts. I'll spin up a runner pool labeled `redwood-fallback`.

Chris (deploy): I'll prepare an alternate workflow that prefers `runs-on: [self-hosted, redwood-fallback]`. But private @redwood packages are only on github.pkg. Need a way to supply those tarballs.

Lisa (platform): I can assemble a temporary npm proxy. I'll pull last-successful package tarballs from our build-cache and host them behind Verdaccio backed by S3. ETA ~25m.

Olivia (support): Opened escalation with GitHub Support (ticket GH-61234). They acknowledged and are investigating DNS/CDN issues for Packages/Actions.

Incident Bot: GitHub status updated to 'Partial Outage' - Actions & Packages. See incident page.

Raj (eng-sre): Runners spun up: 3 GCP VMs registered to org as `redwood-fallback`. They reach github.com but DNS to npm.pkg.github.com still times out. Needs package mirror.

Lisa (platform): Temporary registry live: https://npm-internal.redwood/ (verdaccio -> S3). Scoped @redwood packages pushed there from cache. I updated a throwaway `.npmrc` for CI to use this registry.

Chris (deploy): Kicked off manual run on self-hosted runner. Build logs show `Fetching @redwood/core from https://npm-internal.redwood/` succeeded. Build passed through compile and test. GH artifacts upload failed (GH artifacts service still flaky). Switching artifact uploads to GCS via gsutil as a workaround.

Emma (oncall): Good progress. Consolidated mitigation plan: 1) route CI to self-hosted runners 2) use verdaccio/S3 mirror for private packages 3) avoid GH artifacts service (upload to GCS) 4) push container images directly to GCR and deploy via kubectl.

Chris (deploy): Implemented hotfix workflow: push image directly to `gcr.io/redwood/hotfix:20260105-01` and skip GH artifacts. Triggered manual pipeline on fallback runners — image pushed successfully.

Lisa (platform): Verified image, deployed to staging. Initiating a canary to 5% in prod. Monitoring latency, error rates, and logs.

Raj (eng-sre): Canary started at 1929055421. No anomaly in logs or SLI dashboards so far. If stable for 10m, we expand.

Incident Bot: On-call handoff scheduled: Emma handing to Raj at 1929057200. Please update incident timeline and attach playbook links.

Emma (oncall): Handoff completed. I've documented the exact commands and the temporary registry URL (expires in 6h). Maria - please review customer copy.

Maria (product): Reviewed. Added line to status: "We have implemented a temporary deployment workaround to enable hotfix releases while GitHub investigates. If you have an urgent scheduled maintenance, contact support for manual assistance."

Olivia (support): Notifying 3 enterprise customers on the watchlist; offering to run manual deploys for those with active maintenance windows.

Chris (deploy): Full prod rollout to 100% done at 1929056800. Post-deploy checks green. Rollback steps prepared.

Raj (eng-sre): Continuing to monitor. GitHub status shows intermittent recovery but package registry still degraded. Keeping fallback infra live for now.

Incident Bot: Incident P-4592 state updated to: Mitigated (workaround deployed: self-hosted runners + internal registry). Please attach postmortem and timeline.

Emma (oncall): Closing active pager for initial responder. Please add the commands used to the doc for the postmortem. Snippets below for posterity:

```
# register self-hosted runner
./config.sh --url https://github.com/redwood-inference --token REDACTED --labels redwood-fallback

# temporary .npmrc for CI
registry=https://npm-internal.redwood/
@redwood:registry=https://npm-internal.redwood/

# push image directly
docker build -t gcr.io/redwood/hotfix:20260105-01 .
docker push gcr.io/redwood/hotfix:20260105-01

# manual deploy
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/api api=gcr.io/redwood/hotfix:20260105-01
kubectl rollout status deployment/api
```

Maria (product): I'll publish the status update and include the workaround details.

Olivia (support): GitHub replied: "Investigating DNS/CDN issues affecting Packages & Actions. No ETA." We'll keep the incident open until resolved.

Raj (eng-sre): We'll schedule teardown of fallback runners & verdaccio in 8 hours if GH recovers; otherwise extend TTL. Added ACLs and audit logs.

Emma (oncall): Thanks everyone. Passing monitoring to Raj for overnight watch. I'll lead the postmortem write-up tomorrow. :white_check_mark:"
